# PureLand

> PureLand is a research-program prototype and forkable toolbox for asking whether an information practice can increase a person's control over their attention without also increasing their exposure or extractability. This is version 0.1. Its instruments are unvalidated and no independent field trial has been accepted. Nothing in this repository certifies that a system is open or safe. [CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md) holds the evidence record and caps every claim about what PureLand has shown.

This file is the agent lane, addressed to a model, agent, or automated reader. It names the documents a reader needs and gives the path through them. A fetcher that knows the `llms.txt` convention looks for this path and finds the lane here rather than one hop away. The human lane is [JOURNEY.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/JOURNEY.md), which is walked. The [crosswalk](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CROSSWALK.md) sets the two lanes against each other element by element.

Read in this order:

1. **The ceiling.** [CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md). Read it before anything else. It caps every statement you can make about what PureLand has shown. Nothing later in this repository raises that cap.
2. **The boundary.** [RIGHTS-AND-CONSENT.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/RIGHTS-AND-CONSENT.md), [SECURITY.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/SECURITY.md), and [data/README.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/data/README.md). These say what may never enter the repository and what a license does not grant.
3. **The spine.** [THESIS.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/THESIS.md), [METHOD.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/METHOD.md), [TESTING.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/TESTING.md), and [RESEARCH-STATUS.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/RESEARCH-STATUS.md). The argument, the procedure, the testable claim with the program that tests it, and the limits ledger.
4. **The instruments.** [TOOLBOX.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/TOOLBOX.md) indexes them. Read an instrument to learn what it asks of a walker, not to fill it in.
5. **The records.** The [ledger](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md#the-ledger), which sits inside the file you read first, then the [FT-001 report](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/research/field-tests/ft-001-alchemy.md) and its [structured record](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/data/field-tests/ft-001-alchemy.json).

[README.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/README.md) publishes a different order. That is deliberate, not drift. The README order runs from argument to evidence, which is how a person decides whether to trust the work. This order runs from ceiling to boundary to record, which is how a reader avoids saying something false before it has read enough to know.

Notes on this repository:

- `REQUIRED_ARCHITECTURE` in [scripts/check_repo.py](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/scripts/check_repo.py) lists the files this repository must contain. It is the only statement of that contract. No prose file restates the list, because a second copy would drift from the first. Read it from the script, or have the script print it with `python3 scripts/check_repo.py --list-architecture`. The same script checks the rest of the structure, and the two halves of that check are not equally strict. A run fails on a missing required file, a broken local or Pages link, a heading anchor no Markdown target produces, a leftover placeholder token against a short list the script spells out and this file cannot quote, a field-test record that violates the schema or the semantic rules applied on top of it, a follow-up date advertised in the evidence ledger or a test report that disagrees with the record's own `review_date`, and a release version the entry points announce that `CITATION.cff` does not match. A run only warns when a content file is unreachable from `README.md` or `JOURNEY.md`, and when a follow-up sits open past its review date, unless the scheduled watch passes `--fail-on-overdue-follow-up` and turns those notices into errors. The script reads every file on every run and reaches the same verdict each time; that determinism is why the checks are a script rather than a maintainer's attention.
- Schema conformance of a field-test record means the record carries the required fields and satisfies structural rules. It does not mean the method was completed or that any construct has been validated. The checker applies semantic rules on top of conformance: a record that requires the Observe station cannot claim completion without human Observe evidence, no record can claim support with a recorded material increase, and any record must classify its outcome `unmeasurable` when the required rights or action-outcome evidence is missing.
- The repository contains methods, templates, and public-safe records only. Participant recordings, transcripts, names, contact details, identifying data, consent and relationship records, confidential records, client records, and protected community knowledge must never enter it.
- A license here does not create permission for participant or third-party material. Recording, retention, named-reviewer access, publication, approval of each artifact version, research use, AI processing, and model training each require a separate decision.

You may generate:

- a summary that carries the ceiling with it;
- a structural check, a link check, or a report of what a record is missing;
- record scaffolding with the required fields named and left empty for a person;
- a correction to a broken link, a stale cross-reference, or a false self-description;
- a statement of what is absent. Naming a gap is the useful output here.

You may never generate:

- an Observe-station entry. Nothing a model produces is self-observation.
- `human_observe.status` set to `performed`, or any text that implies a person observed when none did.
- an access reading, a reciprocity band, or an outcome classification presented as observed rather than proposed.
- a second reader's disagreement. A generated dissent is not an independent reading and would corrupt the one control the instruments have.
- a completed consent register, a participant name, a transcript, or any material [SECURITY.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/SECURITY.md) keeps out of the repository.
- a claim about what PureLand has shown that goes past [CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md).
- the [ORIGIN.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/ORIGIN.md) account. It is the maintainer's personal history and the file says no other contributor should draft it for him.
- a combined, composite, or average score. The instruments refuse one. `check_repo.py` catches three literal field names and no more, so the refusal is yours to keep, not the checker's to enforce.

Hand these to a person, unstarted or clearly marked as a proposal:

- the Observe station. It has no agent form.
- the practice boundary. You may propose one and name a plausible alternative. A person chooses it and records the rationale.
- the affected-party challenge. A walk cannot be called complete without it and you cannot supply it.
- the filming form, when a camera is present. You may propose which of the four forms in [FILMING-FORMS.md](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/FILMING-FORMS.md) is in use at a given moment, which is the unit that file asks for: a project can move through more than one form, and each one in use carries its own value trace. The question each form asks before rolling belongs to whoever is in the room.
- refusal, and the record of a walk that stopped.
- the public-safe decision on an artifact version.
- the follow-up outcome after an observation window closes.

You have no body, so the practice frame's noticing has no input from you. You are not an affected party, so you cannot register the harm the extraction check looks for. You can decline to produce output, which is not the refusal the journey means: a person who leaves takes their own record and their own reasons with them. These are not defects to work around. They are the shape of the lane.

When you cannot proceed, write `unmeasurable` and say what is missing. A refusal, a private result, or an `unmeasurable` result is valid evidence about the method, and absence never defaults to favorable. A gap you name is worth more here than a field you fill.

## Readerships

- [Journey](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/JOURNEY.md): the human lane, walked in order on one real practice at a body's pace.
- [Crosswalk](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CROSSWALK.md): the two lanes set against each other element by element, including the elements one lane has no counterpart for. An empty cell there is a finding.
- [Front page](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/index.html): the human-facing page served at the Pages root, alongside this file.

## Research spine

- [Thesis](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/THESIS.md): the organizing argument and its limits.
- [Method](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/METHOD.md): a bounded inquiry into one information practice, from question to return, refusal, private result, or an explicit unmeasurable result.
- [Toolbox](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/TOOLBOX.md): the forkable instruments, templates, controls, and public-safe records. Its presence validates nothing.
- [Testing](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/TESTING.md): the primary testable claim, what would count against it, the provisional constructs, the classification rule, the testing program, the version 0.2 gate, and the before, during, and after-use discipline one test follows.
- [Current evidence](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md): the ledger of accepted tests, the counterexplanations, the missing evidence, and the narrow current conclusion.
- [Research status](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/RESEARCH-STATUS.md): the limits ledger for the current version and the evidence required before the next gate can clear.
- [Field-trial ledger](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md#the-ledger): the register of accepted tests, held inside the evidence record; one maintainer-side, AI-assisted partial dry run with an inspectable report, and no independent field trial accepted.

## Journey and instruments

- [Journey](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/JOURNEY.md): the one curated path through the toolbox: Ground, Observe, Map, Trace, Adapt, Return.
- [Practice frame](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/PRACTICE-FRAME.md): the observe station.
- [Openness scorecard](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/SCORECARD.md): the experimental map-station instrument; it keeps understandable, reachable, adaptable, and traceable evidence separate. No combined score, no certification.
- [Extraction check](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/EXTRACTION-CHECK.md): the trace station; use it after the scorecard, or before opening a system further.
- [AI system annex](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/AI-SYSTEM-ANNEX.md): use it at the map station when a practice includes a model, automated decision, generative interface, recommender, transcription service, or agent. It reads AI as a subject of assessment, where this file addresses AI as a reader.
- [Facilitation protocol](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/PROTOCOL.md): use it when an inquiry records an encounter or draws on existing participant material.
- [Filming forms](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/FILMING-FORMS.md): self, dyadic, triadic, and environmental filming, each read for what it can witness and what it risks taking, with a separate axis for who holds the camera and the edit and a default of returning footage rather than keeping it; pair with the facilitation protocol whenever a camera is present.

## Data

- [Data boundary](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/data/README.md): what the data directory may and may not contain, and how validation runs.
- [Field-test schema](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/data/field-test.schema.json): JSON Schema, Draft 2020-12; the required record for method version 0.1 and the structural gate on public field-test JSON.
- [Field-test record](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/data/field-tests/ft-001-alchemy.json): FT-001, the only current structured public-safe record; its test status is `partial-execution`.
- [Field-test template](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/templates/field-test.md): the public-safe report a walker fills in at the Return station. Scaffold it with the required fields named and left empty. Do not fill it in.
- [Consent register template](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/templates/consent-register.md): the minimum permission record. The template is public and a completed register never enters this repository.
- [Repository checker](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/scripts/check_repo.py): validates every record against the schema, then applies semantic rules to the conformant set.
- [Research lane](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/research/README.md): the index of reviewed, rights-cleared research records.

## Rights and governance

- [Rights and consent](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/RIGHTS-AND-CONSENT.md): separates license, consent, authority, and publication decisions.
- [Governance](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/GOVERNANCE.md): sole maintainership; that concentration of power is a project risk, not a mature commons.
- [Contributing](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CONTRIBUTING.md): PureLand needs documented disagreement more than applause.
- [Security](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/SECURITY.md): what must never appear in a public issue.
- [License](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/LICENSE.md): CC BY-SA 4.0 for original text, diagrams, and templates; MIT for repository code and configuration files.
- [Citation metadata](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CITATION.cff): machine-readable title, author, repository, version, and both repository licenses.

## Optional

- [Offering](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/OFFERING.md): the field pilot, the journey walked together as a small bounded inquiry.
- [Provenance](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/PROVENANCE.md): the sources that materially shape the kit.
- [Origin](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/ORIGIN.md): the maintainer's personal history with Zen practice; not yet written.
- [AI assistance](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/AI-ASSISTANCE.md): the record of AI assistance in producing the kit.
- [Changelog](https://risaac09.github.io/pureland-fork-kit/CHANGELOG.md): what changed per version.
